messages:
Maria Chen: Quick follow-up from the authz RFC — I sketched a migration plan for mapping service identities to project-scoped roles. Need feedback on edge cases (cross-project calls, shared infra svc accounts).

Kevin Park: do you mean mapping API keys to projects or using service tokens?

Maria Chen: both. short version: 1) keep existing API keys but scope them to org/project via metadata; 2) new option: issue short-lived S2S JWTs for inter-service calls. default route: validate via authn service.

Sophie Li: +1 for short-lived tokens. How do we handle legacy keys used by infra agents? We can't rotate them immediately.

Raj Patel: Proposal: accept legacy API keys only for read-only endpoints and require token exchange for write endpoints. Also add `x-project-id` header validation + RBAC layer.

Kevin Park: config snippet I had in mind:
```
server:
  auth:
    legacy_api_keys:
      allowed_scopes: [read]
    s2s_jwt:
      issuer: auth.redwood
      ttl: 5m
```

Sophie Li: audit point: include `actor_id`, `actor_type` (svc/user), `auth_method`, `project_origin` in logs. Example event schema:
```
{"ts":"...","actor_id":"svc-123","actor_type":"service","method":"s2s_jwt","project":"proj-foo","action":"generate"}
```

Maria Chen: cross-project calls: default deny, but add explicit `trust` relationship object between projects (org admin configured). We should avoid implicit escalation via shared API keys.

Kevin Park: what about rate limiting and costing per-project if svc calls cross project? we need billing attribution.

Raj Patel: attribute by effective project header (validated). If invalid, attribute to service owner org and flag for review.

Sophie Li: we should add a migration route: 30-day soft block: log + warn -> 7-day hard block for legacy keys.

Infra-bot: deploy queued: authn-service v2.3.1 -> staging (build 8123)

Maria Chen: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with these decisions. @kevin @sophie @raj please ack or add comments by EOD.

Kevin Park: ack

Sophie Li: ack :+1:

Raj Patel: ack
